newsitem.title: JAPAN: Economy recovering gradually, gaining strength - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Economy recovering gradually, gaining strength - BOJ.

text.p: Japan's economy is recovering gradually and the recovery is becoming firmer, Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita said in a speech on Friday.
"The economy is gradually recovering and the firmness of the recovery has been gaining strength," Matsushita said.
He added that external demand had stopped falling due to the yen's weakening from the latter half of last year and had been rising recently.
Matsushita said inventory adjustments seemed to have been completed and added that the speed in the rise in production had accelerated recently.
He also said that private consumption was on an upward trend and a recovery in capital spending was spreading to many areas of industry.
Matsushita said that the positive mechanism of a rise in production bringing about fresh capital spending and consumption was gradually becoming clearer.
But he added the fall in Japanese stock prices and interest rates from the end of last year showed that financial markets were still uncertain about the outlook for the economy.
He said financial markets were concerned about the effect that fiscal tightening measures to be introduced from April would have on the economy.
Japan plans to raise its sales tax from three to five percent from April 1.

"It is inevitable that the economy will slow down from spring towards summer, but looking at the strengthening of the positive mechanisms, the economy is highly likely to stick to a recovery path," the governor said.

He said that domestic prices had shown little sign of moving onto a clear rising trend but added that the central bank needed to watch prices carefully as import prices had risen sharply recently and as the likelihood of a sustainable recovery was becoming stronger.
Matsushita also said that the BOJ would watch to see whether the rise in the sales tax would trigger inflation.
He said the BOJ would continue to conduct monetary policy with the aim of strengthening the basis of Japan's economic recovery.
He added that the bank would watch movements in financial markets as well as firms' business plans to see whether the recovery would continue.
